source_caption:
The Irishman — Loyalty, Power & Regret

The Irishman (2019) follows Frank Sheeran, a World War II veteran who becomes involved in organized crime and rises through the ranks as a trusted hitman. His connection with crime boss Russell Bufalino eventually brings him into the world of powerful figures whose influence extends far beyond the streets.

Frank's life changes when he becomes closely connected to Jimmy Hoffa, the influential labor leader known for his strong personality and powerful position. As Frank balances his loyalty to Hoffa with his obligations to the criminal organization, he finds himself caught between two worlds that are slowly moving toward conflict.

As tensions rise, Frank is forced to make decisions that will affect everyone around him. His loyalty is tested, friendships begin to break apart, and the consequences of his choices follow him for decades.

The film explores themes of loyalty, betrayal, power, friendship, and regret. Rather than glorifying the criminal lifestyle, it shows the loneliness and personal cost that can come from spending a lifetime serving powerful people.

What makes The Irishman compelling is watching Frank look back on his life and realize that the choices he made for loyalty and survival came with consequences he could never escape.

💬 He spent his life proving his loyalty to powerful men—only to discover what that loyalty would ultimately cost him.

source_details.synopsis: The Irishman (also known as I Heard You Paint Houses) is a 2019 American gangster film directed and produced by Martin Scorsese from a screenplay by Steven Zaillian, based on the 2004 book I Heard You Paint Houses by Charles Brandt. It stars Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, and Joe Pesci, with Ray Romano, Bobby Cannavale, Anna Paquin, Stephen Graham, Stephanie Kurtzuba, Jesse Plemons, and Harvey Keitel in supporting roles. The biographical film follows Frank Sheeran (De Niro), a truck driver who becomes a hitman involved with mobster Russell Bufalino (Pesci) and his crime family before later working for Jimmy Hoffa (Pacino), a powerful Teamster.
